children.name: Vertigo nitidula
children.description: Measurements (Fig. 2). 57 specimens from 13 populations (n = 1 – 18 per population): shell height: 1.50 – 2.20 mm, mean 1.85 + 0.18 mm; shell diameter: 0.90 – 1.15 mm, mean 1.03 + 0.06 mm. Species delimitation. V. nitidula is similar to V. substriata (Jeffreys, 1833) (Fig. 1 P – V), but differs from this species in the finer radial sculpture on the upper whorls, which are ribbed in V. substriata, and the only moderately convex whorls. Moreover, most specimens of V. nitidula are more elongated than specimens of V. substriata. The shell variability within V. nitidula is high. The varieties Pupa sieversi var. punctum Boettger, 1879 (Fig. 1 C) and Pupa sieversi var. subalpestris Boettger, 1880 (Fig. 1 D) were based on differences in shell shape and the development of the angular lamella. However, these as well as other variations of shell characters are not characteristic for specific geographic regions. Shell size and shape vary continuously (Fig. 2). Different shell shapes and the presence or absence of angular lamella and basal fold are found in various combinations and different forms can co-occur within a single population (see Fig. 1 H – J and K – O). Thus, we cannot split this complex into smaller entities and place the named varieties in the synonymy of V. nitidula.
